Course Schedule

Milestones are due Sunday 11:59 PM PT; handoffs to the CSS 553 partner are due Wednesday 11:59 PM PT.

Wk S Topic Reading Due
Part I: The Human
1 A Usability and user-centered design: ISO 9241-11 (effectiveness, efficiency, satisfaction), the UCD lifecycle, UX in agile teams. The course system and the project ID introductory and process chapters; CT Usability and User-Centered Design
1 B The human as information processor: perception, attention, working and long-term memory, the Model Human Processor. ICA: measure your own reaction time and memory span ID cognitive aspects; CT The Human as Information Processor; Miller (1956) Survey; teams and partners set (Fri Apr 2)
2 A Predictive models: Fitts' law, Hick–Hyman law, KLM and GOMS CT Predictive Models; Card, Moran & Newell (1980)
2 B A first experiment: hypothesis, independent and dependent variables, within-subjects design, regression. Lab 1 (Fitts' law) CT Controlled Experiments §1; Fitts (1954) P0 (Sun Apr 11)
Part II: Understanding Users
3 A Surveys and questionnaires: question types, scales, wording bias, sampling, response rates, standard instruments. ICA: fix a bad survey ID data gathering; CT Surveys and Questionnaires; Krosnick (1999) Lab 1
3 B Interviews and contextual inquiry; affinity diagramming CT Interviews and Contextual Inquiry; Beyer & Holtzblatt (1995)
4 A Task analysis: HTA, GOMS decomposition, task flows; personas and scenarios. Lab 2 (HTA and KLM) ID discovering requirements; CT Task Analysis
4 B From findings to requirements: usability scenarios in six-part form; what engineers need to build for usability (undo, cancel, progress) CT Quality-Attribute Scenarios (usability sections); CT Usability-Supporting Architecture; Bass, John & Kates (2001) H1 scenarios to partner (Wed Apr 21); P1 (Sun Apr 25)
Part III: Designing
5 A Design principles: gulfs of execution and evaluation, signifiers, mapping, feedback, constraints; slips and mistakes; visual hierarchy, Gestalt, information architecture ID conceptualizing interaction; CT Design Principles Lab 2
5 B Midterm (Weeks 1–4, 75 min)
6 A Prototyping: fidelity, sketching, paper and Wizard of Oz, interactive prototypes; design critique ID design and prototyping; CT Prototyping and Design Critique
6 B Accessibility: WCAG 2.2 principles and AA criteria, assistive technology, inclusive design. ICA: audit a page with a screen reader CT Accessibility H2 prototype to partner (Wed May 5); P2 (Sun May 9)
Part IV: Evaluating
7 A Inspection methods: heuristic evaluation, severity ratings, aggregating evaluators; cognitive walkthrough ID inspections; CT Inspection Methods; Nielsen & Molich (1990)
7 B Lab 3 (heuristic evaluation), then class aggregation: how many evaluators find how many problems H3 partner increment arrives (Sun May 16)
8 A Usability testing: think-aloud, task design, success, time, errors, SUS; how many users ID evaluation studies; CT Usability Testing; Nielsen & Landauer (1993); Brooke (1996) Lab 3
8 B Pilot tests in class; teams run 5-user tests of the partner's increment during the week Faulkner (2003) P3, findings to partner (Sun May 23)
9 A Controlled experiments: between- and within-subjects designs, counterbalancing, confidence intervals, t-tests, effect sizes, validity threats CT Controlled Experiments; MacKenzie (2024), experiment chapters, optional
9 B Online experiments: A/B tests, telemetry, sample size, peeking, ethics. Lab 4 (experiment analysis) Kohavi, Henne & Sommerfield (2007)
Part V: Delivering
10 A Reporting findings that engineers act on; usability in agile delivery; design systems (no class if Monday: Memorial Day) ID interaction design in practice Lab 4
10 B P4 presentations; course wrap-up P4 report (Sun Jun 6)
11 Final exam (date and time per UW finals schedule) Final exam
